message.content: {"name": "mortgage_property", "parameters": {"space_key": "VIRGINIA_AVENUE", "public_message": "Mortgaging Virginia.", "private_thought": "Just paid $400 on Oriental; cash $63. From Oriental, next roll deaths: 2=CT hotel $600 (unsurvivable), 8=4RR $200 (5/36), 11=TN 1h $70, 12=NY 1h $80. All mortgages = +$140 to $203, which covers the $200 RR and both orange houses; only snake-eyes still kills me. Brown set cannot hurt p2 ($426, hotels everywhere) so cash > monopoly. p2 will not trade to keep me alive and must not get a free pink completion. Mortgage Virginia ($80) now, then Baltic and Med, then end turn."}}
message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly.

I am p3 with $63 cash after paying $400 rent. I own the brown monopoly but have no houses. p2 has massive monopolies and $426 cash. p1 and p4 are bankrupt.

Building houses on the brown properties would cost $50 each, leaving only $13. Even with one house, the rent would be minimal against p2's hotels. I am weighing whether to trade, mortgage, or end my turn.

Only North Carolina Avenue is unowned. p2's properties are heavily built with hotels and houses, while Kentucky and Illinois are mortgaged. I will likely go bankrupt on my next move.

Mortgaging all three brown properties would raise cash to $203, but it destroys the monopoly. I am now calculating my next roll from Oriental Avenue.

From Oriental Avenue, rolling 2 lands on Vermont with a hotel for $550. Rolling 3 lands on Connecticut with a hotel for $600. Both would bankrupt me immediately. I am now mapping the full board order to see every owned space after Oriental.

I have mapped the full board order. After Oriental Avenue, every space is owned by p2. Rolling 4 lands on St. Charles Place for $30. Rolling 5 lands on States Avenue for $40. Rolling 6 lands on Virginia Avenue for $60. Rolling 7 lands on Tennessee Avenue with one house for $100. Rolling 8 lands on New York Avenue with one house for $120. Rolling 9 lands on Atlantic Avenue with two houses for $160. Rolling 10 lands on Ventnor Avenue with two houses for $180. Rolling 11 lands on Water Works for $150. Rolling 12 lands on B&O Railroad for $200.

Rolling 3 lands on Just Visiting, which is safe. Rolling 4 lands on St. Charles Place for $10 in pink rent, which I can afford. Rolling 5 lands on the Electric Company utility, where rent depends on dice.

Rolling 5 on the Electric Company utility costs $50, which I can afford. Rolling 6 lands on States Avenue for $10 in pink rent. Rolling 7 lands on Virginia Avenue, which is mine and costs nothing. Rolling 8 lands on the Pennsylvania Railroad for $200, which would bankrupt me unless I mortgage first. Rolling 9 lands on St. James Place, where p2 owns the orange monopoly with uneven house counts.

St. James Place costs $28 with the orange monopoly, which I can afford. Rolling 10 lands on Community Chest, which is variable. Rolling 11 lands on Tennessee Avenue for $70, and rolling 12 lands on New York Avenue for $80. Both would bankrupt me without mortgaging.

Rolls 2, 8, 11, and 12 would bankrupt me without extra cash. Rolling 5 on the Electric Company costs $50, which I can afford. Community Chest could be dangerous.

Mortgaging all three brown properties would raise cash to $203. That still leaves the Connecticut hotel at $600 as a fatal hit. The Pennsylvania Railroad, Tennessee Avenue, and New York Avenue would be manageable. Vermont is unreachable this turn.

Mortgaging only Virginia would leave me with $143, which still cannot cover the Connecticut hotel or the railroad. Mortgaging all three properties gives me $203, enough to survive the railroad and the other likely hits. The Connecticut hotel remains a fatal risk on roll 2, but that is only a one-in-thirty-six chance. I will mortgage everything now so I can pay when I roll next turn.

I considered trading Virginia Avenue to p2 for a pink monopoly. That would let them build hotels and make the board even more lethal, so it is a bad move.

Trading is futile. p2 has no incentive to help me survive, and any trade that would save me would be rejected.

Building houses is pointless. The brown rent would be negligible before I die, and it would leave only $13 cash. I will mortgage one property at a time, since the tool only allows one space per action.

I will mortgage Virginia Avenue first for $80, then Baltic Avenue for $30, and finally Mediterranean Avenue for $30. This raises cash to $203 without destroying the brown monopoly.

The Pennsylvania Railroad is the most likely fatal roll, so I will mortgage all three properties now rather than across separate turns. Virginia gives the biggest immediate cash boost.
